- When sentiment is neutral or absent (0.00), model tends to overestimate early in the horizon and underestimates late — apply a slight upward bias to later periods.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50 or above), model often underestimates the peak or fails to capture momentum — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days of the horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00 or below), model tends to overcorrect downward — add a small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to counteract the lagged dip.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., 68.02 → 67.89) are common — cap forecast at 1–2% below the spike peak for the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizons — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., 0.20 or -1.00), model underreacts — increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment unit.
